title: Halve the pretraining batch again, 128 -> 64 records, under the Muon incumbent (more optimizer steps, same wall-clock)
description: Batch-size follow-up to 066-claude's keep, not a backlog P-idea (nearest: none; P02 Muon incumbent context): change only BS 128 -> 64 in 066-claude's pretrain.py, keeping every per-step hyperparameter, so the fixed 300 s buys ~1.6-1.9x more optimizer steps (~7,500-9,000 vs 4,760) at roughly the same ~3.4-4 epochs. 066 beat bs 256 on every seed (+13/+23/+33) without lowering val loss, so if the downstream gain comes from more, noisier Muon updates on the same data rather than from a better pretraining fit, halving again should hand expert iteration a still better starting point until gradient noise or per-step overhead dominates.
hypothesis: 066's gain from bs 256 -> 128 did not come from lower val loss (0.0915-0.0956 vs 0.0912) and showed up in later EI rounds, which points at the optimization path (twice as many fixed-spectral-size Muon updates, more gradient noise, twice the cumulative decoupled weight decay) producing a more RL-adaptable model rather than a better-fit one. If the critical batch for that effect is below 128, bs 64 repeats it: ~1.8x more updates, momentum 0.95 still averages ~20 steps (~1,280 records), and epochs stay ~4 so the handoff is not more overconfident (unlike 002). Step time at 128 was 2.03x shorter than at 256, i.e. still GPU-bound; at 64 the eager per-step launch overhead (~1,500 kernels incl. 21 Newton-Schulz orthogonalizations, plus the per-step lens.max() sync) starts to show, so steps should rise ~1.6-1.9x, not 2x. Counter-risks: gradient noise overtakes the benefit (noisier final checkpoint at the 0.1 LR floor), cumulative weight decay doubles again, the 200-step warmup shrinks to ~2% of the budget, and fewer records seen if overhead dominates.

arch.change: none versus 066-claude: 5 untied fork GPT blocks, d_model 256, 8 heads (head dim 32), d_ff 1024, RoPE base 10000, LayerNorm, GELU, untied embedding/readout
arch.checkpoint_reconstruction: GPT(vocab, 5, 256, 8) from the fork; model.cfg records n_layer=5 and the state dict has blocks.0-blocks.4
arch.kv_cache: one fork KV-cache dict per logical block (5 per sample), unchanged fork code

optimizer.name: split-QKV Muon on hidden matrices and the output readout head.weight throughout; continuous AdamW auxiliary (unchanged from 066-claude)

muon.precision: bf16 Newton-Schulz; fp32 momentum and parameters
muon.shape_scale: sqrt(max(1, rows/columns)) per orthogonalized matrix: Q/K/V each 1, attention output 1, fc1 2, fc2 1, head (99,256) 1
muon.schedule: same warmup/cosine fraction as AdamW; muon_lr = 0.01 * adam_lr / 0.001
muon.parameters: All 20 hidden projection parameters (4 per block x 5 blocks) plus head.weight (99,256; vocab 99, no bias) are in Muon: 21 matrices. Five qkv.weight matrices of shape (768,256) use independent Q/K/V updates, represented as a batch of three (256,256) matrices; proj/fc1/fc2 and head are orthogonalized whole. head is wide (99<256) so it is not transposed and its update has 99 singular values near 1.
muon.license: MIT; full copyright and permission notice retained in pretrain.py
muon.qkv_split: After elementwise Nesterov momentum, reshape each QKV update to (3,256,256); independently Frobenius-normalize and run five batched Newton-Schulz steps; reshape back before applying. No extra learning-rate multiplier. Momentum and weight decay stay elementwise and unchanged.

optimizer.adamw_parameters: emb.weight, all projection biases and LayerNorm parameters (incl. ln_f) throughout; head.weight and hidden matrices never enter pretraining AdamW
optimizer.decay_convention: Muon lr*0.01 equals auxiliary AdamW lr*0.1, preserving incumbent per-update shrinkage at every schedule fraction; head.weight therefore keeps the same per-step multiplicative decay it had under AdamW.
optimizer.clipping: joint global gradient norm 1.0 before both optimizers
optimizer.handoff: standard GPT weights only; pretraining optimizer states are discarded and frozen RL creates its own unchanged AdamW

batch.change: 128 -> 64 records per optimizer step; the only edit to pretrain.py (the BS knob). No LR, warmup-step, momentum, decay or clipping rescaling: all per-step hyperparameters are exactly 066-claude's (and 064-claude's).
batch.consequences: WARMUP stays 200 optimizer steps (roughly half the wall-clock it took at 128, ~2% of the budget); the wall-clock cosine is unchanged; per-step weight decay is unchanged, so total decay over the run grows with the step count again; Muon momentum 0.95 now averages ~20 steps of 64 records (~1,280 records); val_loss is computed in batches of 64 instead of 128 (diagnostic only).

config.init: Exactly 066-claude/064-claude/051: fork default construction with 5 blocks, then orthogonal_ on every 2D block parameter (gain 0.02*sqrt(max(rows, cols))); embedding and readout keep the fork normal(0.02); biases zero. Initial weights per seed identical to 066-claude; data order/shift RNG streams differ because batches are half as large.
